title: 339. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Pythagorean Theorem
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the Pythagorean relationship in a right triangle.
questions.question: In a right triangle with legs \(a\) and \(b\) and hypotenuse \(c\), which equation is true?
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the two legs equals the square of the hypotenuse. Therefore, \(a^2+b^2=c^2\). Option B incorrectly uses a difference instead of a sum.
questions.hint: Identify which side is opposite the right angle.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the hypotenuse of a right triangle given the two legs.
questions.question: A right triangle has legs of length \(6\) and \(8\). What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation:
Use the Pythagorean theorem:
\[
c^2=6^2+8^2=36+64=100.
\]
Thus \(c=\sqrt{100}=10\). The value \(14\) is the sum of the legs, not the hypotenuse.
questions.hint: Square the two legs, add the results, and then take the square root.

questions.learningObjective: Find an unknown leg of a right triangle using the Pythagorean theorem.
questions.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse \(13\) and one leg \(5\). What is the length of the other leg?
questions.explanation:
Rearrange the Pythagorean theorem to find the missing leg:
\[
x^2=13^2-5^2=169-25=144.
\]
Thus \(x=\sqrt{144}=12\). The value \(8\) comes from subtracting \(13-5\), which is not valid here.
questions.hint: Subtract the square of the known leg from the square of the hypotenuse.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs \(9\) and \(12\).
questions.question: A right triangle has legs of length \(9\) and \(12\). What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation:
Use the Pythagorean theorem:
\[
c^2=9^2+12^2=81+144=225.
\]
Thus \(c=\sqrt{225}=15\). The value \(16\) does not satisfy the equation.
questions.hint: This is a common Pythagorean triple; check whether \(9^2+12^2\) is a perfect square.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a triangle with given side lengths is a right triangle.
questions.question: A triangle has side lengths \(7\), \(24\), and \(25\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a right triangle because \(7^2+24^2=25^2\).

options.label: B
options.text: It is not a right triangle because \(7+24>25\).

questions.explanation:
Check the converse of the Pythagorean theorem using the longest side \(25\):
\[
7^2+24^2=49+576=625=25^2.
\]
Since the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides equals the square of the longest side, the triangle is a right triangle. Option B only states the triangle inequality.
questions.hint: Compare the square of the longest side with the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

questions.learningObjective: Use the Pythagorean theorem to find the diagonal of a rectangle.
questions.question: A rectangle has side lengths \(8\) and \(15\). What is the length of its diagonal?
questions.explanation:
The diagonal forms a right triangle with the two sides of the rectangle. Therefore,
\[
d^2=8^2+15^2=64+225=289.
\]
Thus \(d=\sqrt{289}=17\). The value \(23\) is the sum \(8+15\), not the diagonal.
questions.hint: Treat the diagonal as the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

questions.learningObjective: Identify which set of side lengths forms a right triangle.
questions.question: Which set of side lengths forms a right triangle?
questions.explanation:
For the set \(5,12,13\), check the longest side:
\[
5^2+12^2=25+144=169=13^2.
\]
So \(5,12,13\) forms a right triangle. For \(6,7,8\), \(6^2+7^2=36+49=85\), but \(8^2=64\), so it is not a right triangle.
questions.hint: Test the largest side against the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

questions.learningObjective: Use the Pythagorean theorem to find an unknown height in a ladder problem.
questions.question: A ladder \(10\text{ feet}\) long leans against a vertical wall. The base of the ladder is \(6\text{ feet}\) from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation:
The ladder, wall, and ground form a right triangle. The ladder is the hypotenuse, so
\[
h^2=10^2-6^2=100-36=64.
\]
Thus \(h=\sqrt{64}=8\text{ feet}\). The value \(4\) comes from \(10-6\), which is not correct here.
questions.hint: The ladder is the hypotenuse of the right triangle.

questions.concept: Missing Leg in a Right Triangle
questions.learningObjective: Calculate an unknown leg when the hypotenuse and one leg are given.
questions.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse \(26\) and one leg \(10\). What is the length of the other leg?
questions.explanation:
Use the Pythagorean theorem to find the missing leg:
\[
x^2=26^2-10^2=676-100=576.
\]
Thus \(x=\sqrt{576}=24\). The value \(16\) is \(26-10\), which is not the correct leg length.
questions.hint: Subtract the square of the known leg from the square of the hypotenuse.

questions.learningObjective: Recover a missing coordinate from a distance and select the valid branch using an inequality.
questions.question: Points \(A=(1,2)\) and \(B=(4,t)\) are \(5\) units apart. If \(t<2\), what is \(t\)?
questions.explanation:
The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(4-1)^2+(t-2)^2&=25\\
(t-2)^2&=16\\
t&=2\pm4.
\end{aligned}
\]
The possible values are \(-2\) and \(6\). Only \(-2\) satisfies \(t<2\), so A is correct.
questions.hint: Use the distance condition, then check which possible vertical coordinate satisfies the inequality.
